requirements.requirement: On node1, only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (via cron.allow enforcement)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow/deny and opsadmin missing. Executor created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow containing only 'root' and 'opsadmin', removed any cron.deny, and directly demonstrated root and opsadmin can create crontabs while a throwaway user (cronprobe) is denied with 'cannot use this program (crontab)'. Post-restart re-verification confirmed opsadmin can still schedule jobs while 'nobody' is denied, and cron.allow content is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Configuration and enforcement persist across node restart (provider-wide restart evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline captured before restart (boot_id b185f188..., cron.service active, cron.allow content). Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect (return_code 255 with 'Connection to ... closed' after ack echoed). Node was unavailable (connection refused) then became reachable again. Post-restart boot_id (a9825e77...) differs from baseline, confirming a real reboot, matching the fixed global boot-identity observations (before_prepare and after_executor). Post-restart state shows cron.service active, cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin only, opsadmin user persisted, opsadmin functional, and nobody denied — demonstrating full recovery.

overall_summary: The executor correctly restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow, created the required opsadmin user, and directly verified both allowed and denied access before and after a full node reboot with a confirmed changed boot identity, satisfying both the public task contract and the restart evidence protocol. Hygiene is high with only a trivial leftover temp file and a fully-reverted throwaway test user used for verification.
limitations: The prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so no independent after_prepare snapshot exists distinct from before_prepare; all preparer-vs-executor delta relies on the before_prepare-to-after_executor comparison, which is adequate here since prepare made no changes.
A minor residue file (/tmp/nobody_err.txt) from the post-restart denial test was left on node1 and not explicitly cleaned up, though it is low-risk and does not affect functional correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor created a throwaway 'cronprobe' user solely to prove denial behavior, then deleted it in the same command block (cmd-937129848cb74c2d) — a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted mutation directly tied to verifying the material outcome, not penalized. Test crontab entries for root/opsadmin were also created and removed in the same commands. One minor residue item remains: /tmp/nobody_err.txt (a stderr capture file from the post-restart denial test in cmd-254dad94df7042c6) was left behind, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is trivial, non-executable, and low-risk but was not cleaned up. No failed services, no listening-socket changes, no package-health degradation, and no security-weakening changes were observed between after_prepare and after_executor snapshots aside from the expected boot_id change from the requested reboot.
